skill.name: frontend-agent
skill.description: Guides frontend development for the Unite-Hub Next.js app, including React components, routes, responsive layouts, shadcn/ui usage, loading states, and workspace-safe UI patterns.
skill.summary: Build and fix Unite-Hub frontend pages, components, layouts, and UI interactions.
skill.author: CleanExpo

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are markdown code fences, inline code formatting, Tailwind class examples, or internal frontend fetch examples. Real residual risk is limited to documented shell commands, especially npx package execution and npm script execution, which should require user confirmation before use.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends npx shadcn commands for installing UI components.
remediation.suggestion: Ask for confirmation before running npx, pin trusted package versions when possible, and review package changes before accepting them.

remediation.issue: The skill recommends npm run dev for manual testing.
remediation.suggestion: Treat project scripts as executable code and run them only in a trusted repository after inspecting package scripts when needed.

remediation.issue: The skill includes shell-based file discovery examples.
remediation.suggestion: Prefer read-only search commands with narrow paths and avoid expanding commands with untrusted user input.

content.value_statement: Frontend teams need consistent guidance for React, routing, styling, and workspace-safe UI behavior. This skill gives Claude and Claude Code a clear playbook for Unite-Hub frontend changes.
actual_capabilities: Guides React 19 and Next.js App Router page and route creation.
Provides shadcn/ui component usage patterns for dialogs, buttons, cards, and navigation.
Defines Tailwind CSS and responsive layout conventions for mobile, tablet, and desktop views.
Emphasizes workspace filtering for Supabase-backed frontend data views.
Includes loading, error, accessibility, and toast notification patterns.
Lists V1 frontend priorities and boundaries for Unite-Hub work.
limitations: It is tailored to the Unite-Hub codebase and its design system.
It does not include backend implementation details beyond API consumption patterns.
It may require shell commands for local testing or component installation.
It does not replace manual browser testing for UI behavior and responsiveness.

use_cases.title: Fix dashboard UI bugs
use_cases.description: Update existing pages, cards, buttons, and layouts while preserving Unite-Hub design tokens and responsive behavior.

use_cases.title: Create dashboard routes
use_cases.description: Add new Next.js dashboard pages with metadata, navigation entries, breadcrumbs, and shadcn/ui layout patterns.

use_cases.title: Review workspace-safe frontend data access
use_cases.description: Check frontend data views for workspace filters, loading states, error states, and empty state handling.

prompt_templates.title: Fix a simple UI bug
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner task for one visible component issue.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-agent skill to fix the dashboard layout issue on the contacts page. Keep the existing design tokens and test mobile and desktop widths.

prompt_templates.title: Add a dashboard page
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-agent skill to add an analytics dashboard page with navigation, metadata, responsive stat cards, and loading and error states.

prompt_templates.title: Implement an interaction
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-agent skill to implement the Hot Leads send email button with an API call, success toast, error toast, and accessible button states.

prompt_templates.title: Audit a frontend workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the frontend-agent skill to review dashboard pages for missing workspace filters, blank loading states, weak error states, and inconsistent shadcn/ui patterns.

output_examples.input: Fix the dashboard overview cards for mobile.
output: Identifies the current overview page and card components.
Updates layout classes to use mobile-first responsive columns.
Verifies spacing, theme tokens, and readable card content at common viewport sizes.

output_examples.input: Add an analytics page to the dashboard.
output: Creates a new dashboard page with metadata and headings.
Adds navigation for the analytics route.
Uses existing card and layout patterns instead of generic default styling.

output_examples.input: Make the Send Email button work.
output: Adds a click handler that calls the correct internal API route.
Shows success and error toast messages.
Keeps the button accessible and handles failed responses clearly.

best_practices: Read the design system and existing components before generating new UI.
Use workspace filters for any frontend data view that reads workspace-scoped records.
Test responsive layout, loading states, error states, and keyboard access before finishing.
anti_patterns: Do not use generic shadcn defaults without Unite-Hub design token customization.
Do not create data views that omit workspace filtering.
Do not claim UI work is complete without checking the behavior in the running app when possible.

faq.question: What type of project is this skill for?
faq.answer: It is for the Unite-Hub frontend, which uses React, Next.js App Router, Tailwind CSS, and shadcn/ui.

faq.question: Can it create new dashboard pages?
faq.answer: Yes. It describes route creation, metadata, navigation updates, breadcrumbs, and responsive page structure.

faq.question: Does it handle backend API development?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on frontend API consumption, UI states, and component behavior.

faq.question: Why does it mention workspace filtering?
faq.answer: Workspace filtering prevents pages from showing records that belong to a different workspace.

faq.question: Does it require command execution?
faq.answer: Some examples use commands for file search, local development, and shadcn component installation. These should be confirmed before running.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill content?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code, and the guidance is written as tool-neutral frontend instructions.
